Tagline: Swap hospitality shifts in two taps, without the group-chat chaos.
About The Project:
Café and bar staff swap shifts through messy group chats. Messages get buried, managers miss swaps, and people end up working shifts they thought they'd given away.

ShiftSwap is a mobile app where you post a shift you can't work, a colleague claims it, and your manager approves it with one tap. Everyone sees the same up-to-date rota.

What works: posting, claiming and approving swaps, push notifications, and a rota view for each person. We seeded it with a real rota from the café one of us works at, and three of her colleagues tried it on Saturday afternoon. Two said they'd use it instead of WhatsApp; one wanted shifts colour-coded by role, which we added overnight.

What we faked: login is a fixed demo account, and there's no payroll export yet.

Tagline: A browser extension that holds your notifications until you're ready.
About The Project: Notifications from Slack and Gmail arrive one at a time all day. Quiet Hours collects them while you're focusing and delivers one digest at times you choose. It works today in Chrome for Gmail and Slack on the web, with digest times and a VIP list that always gets through. We used it ourselves for the last six hours of the hackathon.

Tagline: The AI-powered, blockchain-secured platform revolutionising personal sustainability.
About The Project:
Climate change is the defining challenge of our generation, and individuals want to help but don't know where to start. Carbon Compass is a next-generation platform that will empower every person on the planet to understand, track and offset their carbon footprint in real time.

Our vision is an ecosystem where AI analyses your purchases, travel and energy use and gives personalised recommendations, while a blockchain ledger makes every offset transparent and tamper-proof. In the future we plan to partner with major retailers, airlines and energy companies so that data flows in automatically, and we will gamify sustainability with collectible tokens that reward green behaviour.

During the hackathon we focused on the vision and the user experience. We designed high-fidelity mock-ups in Figma for the onboarding flow, the dashboard, the offset marketplace and a social leaderboard. We also researched carbon accounting standards and wrote a detailed business plan with three revenue streams.

Our next steps are to build the AI recommendation engine, launch the token and run a pilot with a university. We believe Carbon Compass can be a game-changing tool that disrupts the sustainability industry and helps millions of people live greener lives. We are passionate about this problem and will keep working on it after the event.
Sponsor Prizes: Best Social Impact, Best Use of Data

Tagline: Live accessibility reports for bus stops, from the people who use them.
About The Project:
Wheelchair users can't tell in advance whether a stop's boarding area is blocked, the shelter is flooded or the lift at the interchange is broken. Bus Buddy lets riders report a problem at a stop in under ten seconds and shows reports on a map built from the city's open bus-stop data.

On Friday evening, before we started building, we talked to two wheelchair users from a local disability forum. Their main ask was that reports should expire, because stale reports are worse than none, so every report fades after six hours unless someone confirms it.

What works: the map with all 1,900 stops from the open dataset, reporting, confirming and auto-expiry. Colours and text sizes pass WCAG AA contrast checks. What doesn't yet: there are no accounts, so reports could be spammed.

Tagline: Find a free study room on campus right now.
About The Project: It's hard to find a free study room during exam season. StudySpace shows a list of study rooms and lets students mark a room as busy or free. We built the list page and the toggle. Next we want to add a map and opening hours.

Tagline: Medication reminders that tell family if a dose is missed.
About The Project:
Older people living alone sometimes miss medication, and their families worry. PillPal reminds the user when a dose is due, and if it isn't marked as taken within an hour it texts a family member.

We got the reminder schedule and the 'taken' button working on Android. The text alert isn't finished: it works in the emulator with a test number but crashed on a real phone, and we ran out of time to fix it. We'd like to add photos of each pill so they're easier to tell apart.

Tagline: Spaced-repetition flashcards for the words you actually meet.
About The Project:
This was the first hackathon for three of the four of us! Lingo Ladder lets you paste a paragraph in Spanish, picks out words you probably don't know, and turns them into flashcards that come back on a spaced-repetition schedule.

It works in the terminal and as a simple web page. We learned Flask from scratch this weekend. Word difficulty comes from a frequency list, so common words are skipped. We tried it on a news article: it chose 14 words, and our Spanish-speaking teammate agreed 11 of them were the hard ones.

Tagline: See which subscriptions are quietly eating your student loan.
About The Project:
Upload a CSV export from your bank and Spend Lens finds recurring payments, groups them by merchant and shows what each costs per year. It flags price rises (for example a streaming service that went from £6.99 to £8.99) and free trials that turned into paid plans.

We tested it on our own statements from three different banks. It found 23 recurring payments and we checked each by hand: 21 were correct, one was a monthly transfer to a friend, and one subscription was missed because the merchant's name changed. The app shows these limits rather than hiding them. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: it runs on your own laptop.

Tagline: Snap your fridge, get a recipe.
About The Project:
Take a photo of what's in your fridge and Recipe Remix suggests three recipes using those ingredients. We use a vision API to identify ingredients and a recipe API to find matches.

In our demo it recognised eggs, milk and peppers but thought a courgette was a cucumber, so results depend a lot on lighting. We added a step where you can correct the ingredient list before searching. Our AI is very accurate in most cases.
Built With: React, Node.js, Google Cloud Vision, Spoonacular API

Tagline: The all-in-one platform for discovering, organising and growing communities.
About The Project:
Meetup Mapper is a complete solution for community organisers and members. Users will be able to discover events near them, RSVP, chat with other attendees, split costs, share photos, get AI-generated event recommendations and earn badges for attending. Organisers will get analytics dashboards, ticketing, automated reminders, sponsor management and a CRM.

We spent the first part of the hackathon designing our database schema, which has 18 tables, and planning a microservice architecture with a service for each feature. We set up a Kubernetes configuration and a CI pipeline. We also built a landing page with a sign-up form for our waiting list.

Unfortunately we ran into problems connecting the services, so the main app isn't working yet, but the landing page is live and the architecture is ready to scale to millions of users. We have a clear roadmap and plan to launch next semester.
Built With: React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Docker, GitHub Actions

Tagline: A soil sensor that tells you when your plant is actually thirsty.
About The Project: We built a moisture sensor from an Arduino and a capacitive probe that posts a reading every minute to a small dashboard. When the soil gets too dry it sends a notification. It's working on the bench with a real basil plant, and we calibrated the dry and wet readings with a cup of water. The case is a 3D-printed prototype.

Tagline: Share your walk home with friends, without sharing your location all day.
About The Project:
SafeWalk lets you start a walk, pick two friends, and share your live route only until you arrive. If you stop moving for more than five minutes or go off route, your friends get an alert with your last location.

Live sharing and arrival detection work in our demo across two phones. The off-route alert works in the simulator. We asked five students in our accommodation how they get home at night; four already text a friend when they leave and when they arrive, which is the habit we built around.
Built With: React Native, Google Maps API, Firebase
